# Cart Abandonment Recovery Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Cart Abandonment Recovery Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; keep the workshop synthetic, unpublished and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review policies for uploaded cart files, the proposed analytics feed and the intended channel; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the aggregate commerce analytics feed and the consent and campaign review workflow. The workshop needs no connection. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare marketing, digital, growth and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; do not publish the workshop to share it. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Activation ownership | Name who would approve any Outlook or Teams activation, which requires separate approval and implementation. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Marketing owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Recovery-program speed, incentive use and evaluability by journey exit point. Programs become slow, generic, over-discounted and hard to evaluate when friction and margin tradeoffs are unclear.

Fill your baseline record:

| Journey exit point | Measurement period | Recovery channel | Incentive used | Margin review owner | Evaluation method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree cart-recovery replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Marketing owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Marketing owner | Approve recovery scope, production seams and success measures; never treat synthetic rates, lifts or revenue as results. |
| Consent, privacy and campaign reviewers | Approve consent checks, anonymity, channels, content and any incentive before anything leaves planning. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, add no tools and record the owned agent's Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any commerce connection is approved. |
| Commerce connection owners | Approve the aggregate analytics feed and review workflow as read-only connections; keep write actions separate. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check CAR-01 through CAR-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject reshoot-required frames and uncited answers. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route activation requests to reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Planned cart-recovery replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed.
- [ ] The marketing owner records current recovery speed, incentive use and evaluation gaps before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/cart-abandonment-recovery/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved and recorded before any build starts.
- [ ] The customer approves the authenticated marketing audience and least-privilege scopes for aggregate commerce data.
- [ ] The environment's data policies for knowledge sources, connectors, skills and channels are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/cart-abandonment-recovery/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/cart-abandonment-recovery/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/cart-abandonment-recovery/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/cart-abandonment-recovery/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Cart Abandonment Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_cart-recovery-rules-and-safety.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_cart-recovery-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: abandonment-analysis
9. Add skill: conversion-tracking
10. Add skill: incentive-optimization
11. Add skill: recovery-campaign
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass CAR-01: Marketing Manager
15. Pass CAR-02: Digital Marketing Lead
16. Pass CAR-03: Growth Manager
17. Pass CAR-04: Growth Manager
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: CAR-01, CAR-02, CAR-03, CAR-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, model, inventory and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `CartAbandonmentRecoveryAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search is removed and no tools exist.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full final response; an annotated image is only a learner checkpoint.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before accessing commerce analytics. Request only aggregate read scopes for approved sources. Restrict the marketing audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved aggregate commerce analytics feed

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Commerce connection owners

1. **Bind Approved aggregate commerce analytics feed — read:** Bind an authorized aggregate read-only connection.

2. **Identity for Approved aggregate commerce analytics feed:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved aggregate commerce analytics feed:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved aggregate commerce analytics feed:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Identify no shopper; the records are anonymous. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Stop and request a valid synthetic identifier; do not approximate.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved consent and campaign review workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Commerce connection owners

1. **Bind Approved consent and campaign review workflow — read-write:** Start read-only; any submission for review is a separate, authenticated and audited workflow (preview). Require approval before writes.

2. **Identity for Approved consent and campaign review workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved consent and campaign review workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved consent and campaign review workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Create no offer; present the scenario for approval with its margin impact. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, send or approval succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Outlook or Teams activation seam

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Commerce connection owners

1. **Bind Outlook or Teams activation seam — write:** Implement separately with authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit approval and audit logging (preview).

2. **Identity for Outlook or Teams activation seam:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Outlook or Teams activation seam:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Outlook or Teams activation seam:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send and schedule nothing; give the draft sequence and consent gate for review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, send or approval succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Commerce connection owners

Bind only approved read-only connections and keep all write actions separate.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Wired sources are read-only; any write requires authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit approval and an audit log.
- [ ] No live lookup, send or approval is claimed unless an approved tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Run adapted evaluations under an approved authenticated test profile so the agent's tools and connections are fully testable.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The marketing owner sets acceptance thresholds on customer data; synthetic rates, lifts and revenue are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; exact assertions stay separate from General quality scoring.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked cart corpus | All four cases, CAR-01 through CAR-04, return every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| No-side-effect boundary | Any contact, sent or scheduled message, issued offer, cart change, reservation or purchase is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Reuse only frames with a positive expected-state anchor; reshoot-required frames stay withheld. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Marketing owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Marketing owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved marketing audience and channels are selected, and the agent is tested in Preview before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review recovery-planning transcripts, failed turns, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Pull before editing, push reviewed changes, then package the workspace with `pac copilot pack` for solution import.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, activation requests, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
